format: CollarID GPS block v1 test vectors
generator: reference/make_vectors.py (deterministic; do not edit this file by hand)
conventions: All numbers are integers. In decoded output h_acc_m is an integer or null (unknown accuracy); gps_fix_time_s is always an integer in v1.

vectors: gps_block_encode(fixes, header_epoch, cap) must return hex (null = emit nothing), gps_block_bits(fixes, header_epoch) must return bits (0 when N after exclusion is outside 1..32), and decode(hex, header_epoch) must return ok with decoded, oldest first.
cap is the cap passed to gps_block_encode: 180 (the nanopb max_size) unless the vector tests the cap itself.
decoded is [] when hex is null. hex_uncapped (only when the cap alone refused) is the block the layout gives without a cap; the decoder does not enforce the cap and must decode it.
A fix may omit h_acc_dm (unknown accuracy, like 0) or ttff_s (read as 0).
note (vectors) and why (decoder_only) are free text for humans; tests ignore them.
decoder_only: decode(hex, header_epoch) must give expect: "ignored", "empty", or ok with that list of fixes.
Every track is synthetic, at fictional locations. Times are 2027 or later, except the clock-gate and range-limit cases, which sit on the constants 1767225600 (2026-01-01) and 2^32-1. No field data.

vectors.name: single_fix
vectors.note: N = 1: ttff0 is sent instead of max/rest.

vectors.name: n2_identical_positions
vectors.note: Same position, two times: lat_w = lon_w = 0, no delta bits.

vectors.name: n3_identical_fixes_129_bits
vectors.note: Three identical fixes and age 1: 129 bits, so the block is 17 bytes with 7 pad bits (one bit past a byte boundary).

vectors.name: stationary_jitter_n12
vectors.note: Resting animal, 5-min fixes: position noise only.

vectors.name: moving_track_n12
vectors.note: Travelling animal, 5-min fixes.

vectors.name: southern_western_hemisphere
vectors.note: Negative latitude and longitude throughout.

vectors.name: half_step_positive
vectors.note: lat_e7 and lon_e7 end in 50: q rounds half up (123456750 -> 123456800).

vectors.name: half_step_negative
vectors.note: Negative half step rounds up too: -123456750 -> -123456700.

vectors.name: negative_floor_not_truncation
vectors.note: -123456751 -> -123456800 by floor division; C truncation would give -123456700.

vectors.name: equal_timestamps
vectors.note: Four fixes with one timestamp: the decoder returns them in input order.

vectors.name: unsorted_input
vectors.note: Input out of time order; decoded comes back oldest first.

vectors.name: unsorted_with_ties
vectors.note: Out of order with a three-way tie: decoded is a stable ascending sort of the input.

vectors.name: age_zero
vectors.note: header_epoch equals the newest fix time.

vectors.name: age_minus_one
vectors.note: Newest fix one second after header_epoch.

vectors.name: age_large_negative
vectors.note: header_epoch at the clock gate, fix at 2^32-1: age -2527741695, age_w = 33 (its maximum).

vectors.name: age_large_positive
vectors.note: header_epoch 2^32-1, fix at the clock gate: age_w = 33.

vectors.name: header_epoch_zero
vectors.note: Raw header epoch 0 (clock never set) with a real fix time: the fix time still decodes exactly.

vectors.name: antimeridian_crossing
vectors.note: Track crosses +180 to -180; the format does not wrap, the jump costs a wide lon_w.

vectors.name: poles_and_180
vectors.note: Fixes exactly on lat +-90 and lon +-180 (inside the range): lat_w = 26 and lon_w = 27, both at their maximum.

vectors.name: time_width_dtmin_32
vectors.note: Two fixes 2527741695 s apart: dtmin_w = 32 (its maximum).

vectors.name: time_width_dt_32
vectors.note: dt_min 0 and one gap of 2527741695 s: dt_w = 32 (its maximum).

vectors.name: int32_min_excluded
vectors.note: INT32_MIN latitude and INT32_MIN longitude are excluded; the valid fix goes alone.

vectors.name: int32_min_only
vectors.note: Every fix excluded: N = 0, nothing is emitted.

vectors.name: just_outside_range_excluded
vectors.note: lat 900000001 and lon -1800000001 are excluded.

vectors.name: null_island_excluded
vectors.note: An input fix at exactly (0, 0) is excluded.

vectors.name: clock_gate_boundary
vectors.note: t = 1767225599 is excluded, t = 1767225600 is kept.

vectors.name: below_clock_gate_only
vectors.note: The only fix is below the clock gate: nothing is emitted.

vectors.name: near_null_island_excluded
vectors.note: The null island test is on the quantized position: (30, -40) and (-50, 49) quantize to (0, 0) and are excluded; (50, -50) quantizes to (1, 0) and (-51, -99) to (-1, -1) by floor division (C truncation would give (0, 0) and wrongly exclude it); both are kept.

vectors.name: near_null_island_only
vectors.note: The only fix is (49, -49), which quantizes to (0, 0): excluded, nothing is emitted.

vectors.name: n33_one_excluded_is_n32
vectors.note: 33 fixes, one below the clock gate: N = 32, the maximum.

vectors.name: n33_refused
vectors.note: 33 valid fixes: N > 32, nothing is emitted.

vectors.name: ttff_saturation_and_tie
vectors.note: ttff 1022, 1023, 1024, 2^32-1, 5, 2^32-1, 7 (oldest first): max ties at 2^32-1, the newer one (lower wire index) gets ttff_max = 1023; the mean of the rest saturates at 1023.

vectors.name: ttff_tie_lowest_wire_index
vectors.note: ttff 5, 40, 12, 40 (oldest first): the newest 40 is wire index 0 and keeps 40; the older 40 gets the mean of the rest, (5 + 40 + 12) / 3 = 19.

vectors.name: ttff_mean_rounds_half_up
vectors.note: ttff 1, 100, 2: the rest mean 1.5 rounds up to 2.

vectors.name: ttff_single_saturated
vectors.note: N = 1 with ttff 2^32-1: ttff0 = 1023.

vectors.name: ttff_kmax_raw_not_saturated
vectors.note: Wire-order ttff 1500, 3000, 10: kmax compares the RAW values, so kmax = 1 and the rest mean is (1500 + 10) / 2 = 755. Comparing saturated values (1023, 1023, 10) would tie and give kmax = 0.

vectors.name: ttff_saturated_tie_not_raw_tie
vectors.note: Wire-order ttff 1024, 1025, 1023, 5: the saturated values tie at 1023 on wire 0..2 (lowest index 0), the raw maximum is wire 1. kmax = 1; the rest mean (1024 + 1023 + 5) / 3 rounds to 684.

vectors.name: ttff_absent_is_zero
vectors.note: The middle fix has no ttff_s: it is read as 0. Wire-order ttff 30, 0, 9: kmax = 0, and the rest mean (0 + 9) / 2 rounds up to 5.

vectors.name: ttff_absent_single
vectors.note: N = 1 without ttff_s: ttff0 = 0.

vectors.name: realistic_n5_5min
vectors.note: Five 5-min fixes, the old per-packet limit.

vectors.name: realistic_n12_hourly_5min
vectors.note: Hourly uplink of 5-min fixes, grazing animal.

vectors.name: realistic_n24_hourly_150s
vectors.note: Hourly uplink of 2.5-min fixes at 84 N (lon deltas are 10x wider in 1e-5 deg than at the equator).

vectors.name: realistic_n24_2h_5min
vectors.note: Two hours of 5-min fixes.

vectors.name: vehicle_n24_near_cap
vectors.note: Translocation by vehicle inside a 24-fix window of ~27-min fixes, with a 3-hour gap: lat_w 14, lon_w 16, dt_w 14, like the largest real block (160 B).

vectors.name: moving_n32_over_cap
vectors.note: 32 fixes of a fast mover at 84 N: the block needs more than 180 B, so the encoder refuses (hex null) and the caller drops fixes. hex_uncapped is the block without a cap.

vectors.name: cap_exact_fit
vectors.note: cap equal to the block length: emitted.

vectors.name: cap_one_short
vectors.note: cap one byte short: refused, never truncated.

decoder_only.name: zero_length
decoder_only.why: An empty gps_block carries no fixes; not an error.

decoder_only.name: one_byte
decoder_only.why: Version 1, N = 1, then nothing: read past end.

decoder_only.name: truncated_header
decoder_only.why: First 5 bytes of a valid 3-fix block.

decoder_only.name: truncated_last_byte
decoder_only.why: A valid 3-fix block without its last byte.

decoder_only.name: nonzero_padding
decoder_only.why: A valid block with its last pad bit set.

decoder_only.name: extra_trailing_byte
decoder_only.why: A valid block plus one 0x00 byte.

decoder_only.name: version_0
decoder_only.why: Version 0 is reserved and invalid.

decoder_only.name: version_2
decoder_only.why: A v1 body under version 2: not implemented, ignored.

decoder_only.name: version_7
decoder_only.why: Version 7: ignored.

decoder_only.name: valid_three_fixes
decoder_only.why: The unmodified base block of this section.

decoder_only.name: lat0_out_of_range
decoder_only.why: lat0 decodes to q = 9000001 (just past +90).

decoder_only.name: lon0_out_of_range
decoder_only.why: lon0 decodes to q = -18000001 (just past -180).

decoder_only.name: lat0_max_zigzag
decoder_only.why: lat0 = 2^25-1, the largest the field holds.

decoder_only.name: delta_walks_past_pole
decoder_only.why: Newest fix at q_lat 8999995; the delta to the older fix is +10 instead of -10, which puts it at 9000005, past +90.

decoder_only.name: delta_walks_past_180
decoder_only.why: Newest fix at q_lon 17999900; a delta of +101 puts the older fix at 18000001, past +180.

decoder_only.name: ttff_kmax_ge_n
decoder_only.why: N = 3 and ttff_kmax = 3.

decoder_only.name: age_w_34
decoder_only.why: age_w = 34, above its maximum 33.

decoder_only.name: lat_w_27
decoder_only.why: lat_w = 27, above its maximum 26.

decoder_only.name: lon_w_28
decoder_only.why: lon_w = 28, above its maximum 27.

decoder_only.name: dtmin_w_33
decoder_only.why: dtmin_w = 33, above its maximum 32.

decoder_only.name: dt_w_33
decoder_only.why: dt_w = 33, above its maximum 32.

decoder_only.name: t0_below_gate
decoder_only.why: header_epoch = gate + 10 and age 20: newest fix 10 s before the gate.

decoder_only.name: tk_below_gate
decoder_only.why: dt_min raised by 200: the older fix lands 100 s before the gate.

decoder_only.name: t0_above_uint32
decoder_only.why: header_epoch 2^32-1 and age -1: newest fix at 2^32.

decoder_only.name: q_zero_zero_newest
decoder_only.why: N = 1 with lat0 = lon0 = zz(0): the fix reconstructs to q = (0, 0), which the encoder never emits, so the whole block is corrupt.

decoder_only.name: q_zero_zero_after_delta
decoder_only.why: Newest fix at q = (2, 2); deltas of (-2, -2) put the older fix at q = (0, 0): the whole block is corrupt, the newest fix is not returned either.

decoder_only.name: q_zero_one_decodes
decoder_only.why: Control for the two above: the older fix at q = (0, 1) is a valid position and decodes.

decoder_only.name: over_cap_block_still_decodes
decoder_only.why: The N = 32 block that the firmware cap refuses (moving_n32_over_cap): the decoder does not enforce the 180 B cap and decodes it.
